card werk-stack-framework  [decided]
Client framework: React + Vite
why: Criterion 2 (state-preserving per-component HMR) and criterion 6 (agent proficiency) both point at React, and neither runner-up wins them back.

React + Vite. Vite runs as the CLIENT dev server, in middleware mode, inside werk's own Bun server. It is not the server runtime — that is why this does not contradict #werk-hmr, which rejected **vite-node as the process host** after it crashed werk outright (#werk-hmr:src2). One process: Bun serves the API and the SSE stream and hot-reloads its own modules. Vite transforms and hot-reloads the client.

## Why, against the six criteria

1. **Component architecture** — React. Every candidate satisfied this.
2. **Per-component HMR preserving state** — the discriminator. React Fast Refresh preserves hook state per component. It is the most proven implementation of this requirement. Every rejected option lost or weakened it: Lit has no equivalent (#werk-stack:opt0), Solid remounts (#werk-stack:opt2), svelte-hmr is less reliable for the case that matters (#werk-stack:opt3). werk's chat pane holds a live SSE stream and an in-flight turn. A remount on save is the failure this criterion exists to prevent.
6. **Agent proficiency** — React by a wide margin. It ranks alongside criterion 2. It is why the Svelte 5 runner-up lost: runes are recent enough that agents still reach for Svelte 4 store idioms.

Criteria 3, 4, and 5 do not discriminate between frameworks — see #werk-stack-hydration and #werk-hmr.

The three rejected options are #werk-stack:opt0, #werk-stack:opt2, #werk-stack:opt3, each with its own why_not.

  -> refines         werk-stack  The frontend needs a component stack
  -> depends_on      werk-hmr  Rebuild werk's dev server on a stack with HMR that survives its own edits
       why: The client stack runs inside the Bun server with the hot reload that #werk-hmr chose, and avoids its rejected vite-node host.
  <- alternative_to  werk-stack:opt0  Stay vanilla. Add web components or Lit for structure
  <- alternative_to  werk-stack:opt2  SolidJS with Vite
  <- alternative_to  werk-stack:opt3  Svelte 5 with runes, plus Vite

  <- depends_on      werk-test-visual  How the agent drives a real browser
  <- depends_on      werk-mc-reload-storm  Changes made in one tab must not reset other tabs
  <- depends_on      werk-client-reload  In dev, Vite runs inside the werk server, and a client change it cannot apply in place reloads the page

card werk-stack-framework  [decided]
Client framework: React + Vite

I recommend **shadcn/ui**: Radix primitives styled with Tailwind, with the component files copied into the client.

I proposed the ghost card #werk-stack-ui under #werk-stack. It has `who: you`, status open, and a depends_on edge to #werk-stack-framework, which is decided and not stale. Your four requirements are its criteria. These are the options, ranked:

1. **shadcn/ui** (`:opt0`). Agents know it better than any other React component set. The client owns the component files, so a change is an edit to a file. Tailwind compiles to static CSS. The risk: each screen can edit a component instead of passing a variant, and the components then drift apart.
2. **Radix Themes** (`:opt1`). It has the smallest and strictest set: size, colour and variant are props, and it uses plain CSS with no Tailwind. A look that the props cannot give needs a CSS override.
3. **Mantine** (`:opt2`). It uses static CSS modules and has the most ready components. That large set conflicts with "a limited set".
4. **MUI or Chakra** (`:opt3`). I marked it rejected. Both compute styles in JavaScript at run time through Emotion, so both fail the performance criterion.

You can remove the shadcn drift risk with one rule: a screen passes a variant and never edits a shared component file. If you choose shadcn/ui, I add that rule to the decision.

Next: choose one option. I then write `why_not` reasons on the other options and mark the card decided. The card and its four options wait for your ✓.
